symbols.name: chunk count bound
symbols.meaning: The largest number of equal-width address chunks that one layer acts on, so $d$ counts chunks.
symbols.quote: Here $d$ is the largest number of equal-width chunks a layer acts on, and $D \le d$ is the number used in one layer; the letter $D$ changes meaning here.

symbols.name: selected chunk count
symbols.meaning: The number of address chunks used in one layer, each contributing one selected bit; this replaces the earlier meaning of $D$ as an address-field group.
symbols.quote: Here $d$ is the largest number of equal-width chunks a layer acts on, and $D \le d$ is the number used in one layer; the letter $D$ changes meaning here.

symbols.name: cost exponent
symbols.meaning: A fixed exponent below one in the layer's cost bound $O(Vd^{\lambda'})$, chosen above two exponents fixed in the proof.
symbols.quote: Here $\lambda'$ is a fixed exponent below one, chosen above two exponents fixed in the proof, so it measures growth in $d$, not a count.

relations.quote: A simultaneous butterfly layer applies the [butterfly operation](butterfly-operation.md) to one selected address bit of every record at once.

relations.predicate: is formed as the tensor product
relations.quote: The layer is formed as the [tensor product](tensor-product.md) of the butterfly operation on the $D$ selected bits, acting on each coefficient and leaving other address bits unchanged.
The layer computes its chunk moves by the [linear network with restored auxiliary values](linear-network-exchange.md), which exchanges banks of values with prescribed signs.
